mainTopic: Who keeps the נכסי צאן ברזל (guaranteed dowry property) after a divorce, the wife or the husband? A side discussion asks whether being financially responsible for something makes it count as yours, so that a כהן's animals and slaves may eat תרומה.
overview: When a marriage ends, who gets the wife's guaranteed dowry items (נכסי צאן ברזל)? רב יהודה says she takes back the actual items, because they carry the honor of her father's family. רב אמי says the husband keeps them and pays their value, because the משנה says he carries their risk and that is why such slaves eat תרומה. רב ספרא answers that the משנה only says he is responsible for them, not that he owns them. The גמרא tests this with a rented cow and an appraised cow, and concludes that full responsibility, not partial, is what counts for תרומה. Next, a ברייתא is brought for each side, and רב נחמן rules like רב יהודה, because his reason is more sensible. Then comes a story: a widow's fine wool robe was used by the orphans as a shroud for her husband. רבא rules that the dead man has acquired it, since before she collects it the robe is still in the husband's possession. The amud ends as the גמרא starts showing that רבא is following his usual reasoning, with a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute: the items go to her or to him
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the wife can take back her guaranteed dowry items themselves. רב אמי rules that the husband may keep them and pay her their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The law is with her (she takes the items). And רב אמי said: the law is with him (he keeps them and pays).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating a disagreement that began just before this point: who decides what happens to the נכסי צאן ברזל when the marriage ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife wants the actual items, such as slaves, returned to her. The husband wants to keep them and give her their money value. רב יהודה says she wins, and רב אמי says he wins. The next steps explain each side's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is on her side
The law is on his side
Guaranteed dowry property: the husband takes it over at a fixed value and is responsible for that value

phrases.english: The law is with her;
phrases.notes: This finishes רב יהודה's statement, which started just before. She may take back the actual items.

phrases.english: and Rav Ami said: The law is with him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: the wife takes the actual items. רב אמי: the husband keeps them and pays their value.

steps.title: Why רב יהודה sides with the wife
steps.stepSummary: The items are the pride of her father's family, so they really belong to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said the law is with her, because the items are the pride of her father's house, so they are hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב יהודה's reason: these items carry her family's honor, so they count as hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These things came from her parents' home, and her family's reputation is tied to them. So even though the husband held them and was responsible for their value, they still truly belong to her, and she can demand them back as they are.

keyTerms.meaning: The pride or honor of her father's family

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said the law is with her
because of the pride of her father's house;
they are hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב יהודה's side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guaranteed dowry items carry her family's honor, so they belong to her.

steps.title: Why רב אמי sides with the husband
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי points to the משנה. The husband bears the loss if the slaves die and gets the gain if they increase, and because he is responsible for them they eat תרומה. That sounds like they are his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said the law is with him, because the משנה said: if they die, they die at his loss; if they increase, the gain is his. Since he is responsible for them, they may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי brings support from a משנה to show that the guaranteed items belong to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the husband takes all the loss and all the gain on these slaves, and that this is why a כהן's guaranteed slaves eat תרומה. Only things that belong to a כהן eat תרומה, so רב אמי reads this to mean the slaves are his. If they are his, he only owes her their money value.

keyTerms.meaning: If they die, the loss is his
He is responsible for them (he carries the risk)
The portion of produce given to a כהן; only the כהן and what belongs to him may eat it

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said: The law is with him,
since the Master said:
phrases.notes: "The Master" here means the משנה about a woman who brings slaves into her marriage with a כהן.

phrases.english: If they die, they die for him,
and if they increase, they increase for him;
since he is responsible for them, they may eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the opposite side of the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב אמי's ruling that the husband may keep the items and pay their value.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that the husband bears the loss and gain on guaranteed slaves, and that they eat תרומה because he is responsible for them.

steps.title: רב ספרא: responsible does not mean owner
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says the משנה never calls the slaves his. It only says he is responsible for them, and in truth they are not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Does the משנה say 'and they are his'? It says 'since he is responsible for them.' Really, they are not his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא rejects רב אמי's proof by reading the משנה's words more carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה chose the words "since he is responsible for them," not "since they are his." So the slaves eat תרומה because the husband carries their risk, not because he owns them. Ownership stays with the wife, so רב אמי's proof does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach? (pointing out that the text does not say this)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ספרא is not saying the slaves stop eating תרומה. They still eat. He only changes the reason: responsibility, not ownership.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Does it teach "and they are his"?
It teaches "since he is responsible for them,"
but really they are not his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אמי's reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אמי's proof from the משנה, not necessarily his final ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה speaks of responsibility, not ownership, so it cannot prove the slaves belong to the husband.

steps.title: Challenge from the rented cow
steps.stepSummary: Does responsibility alone really let something eat תרומה? A משנה says a כהן who rents an Israelite's cow may not feed it תרומה vetches, even though he must feed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does everything a person is responsible for eat תרומה? But we learned: an Israelite who rented a cow from a כהן may feed it תרומה vetches. A כהן who rented a cow from an Israelite, even though he must feed it, may not feed it תרומה vetches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ספרא's idea that being responsible for something is enough to let it eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the כהן renting the cow has responsibilities, since he even has to feed it, yet he still may not give it תרומה. What matters is who owns the cow. That seems to show that ownership, not responsibility, is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetches (a kind of animal feed) that are תרומה
Its food is his duty to provide

phrases.english: And wherever he is responsible for them,
do they eat תרומה?
But didn't we learn:
An Israelite who rented a cow from a כהן
may feed it vetches of תרומה.
A כהן who rented a cow from an Israelite,
even though its food is his responsibility,
may not feed it vetches of תרומה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן אָכְלִי בִּתְרוּמָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the idea in רב ספרא's reading that responsibility without ownership is enough for תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that being responsible for something lets it eat תרומה even without owning it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן who rents a cow has responsibility, even for feeding it, yet it may not eat תרומה, so ownership must be what counts.

steps.title: A renter is not fully responsible
steps.stepSummary: The rented cow is not a fair comparison. A renter pays for theft and loss, but not for accidents, the cow getting thin, or a drop in its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so? Even if he is liable for theft and loss, is he liable for accidents beyond his control, for the cow getting thin, or for a drop in its value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by showing that a renter's responsibility is only partial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A renter pays only if the cow is stolen or lost. He does not pay for accidents, weakness, or a fall in price. With guaranteed property the husband carries every kind of loss, so the rented cow is a weaker case and proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (rejects the comparison)

phrases.english: And do you really think so?
Granted he is liable for theft and loss,
for its accidents, for its getting thin,
and for a drop in its value, is he liable?
phrases.notes: The answer is clearly no. A renter does not pay for these.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? נְהִי נָמֵי דִּמְחַיֵּיב בִּגְנֵבָה וַאֲבֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison used in the challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the rented cow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A renter is only partly responsible, while guaranteed property puts the full risk on the husband.

steps.title: Guaranteed property is like the appraised cow
steps.stepSummary: The right comparison is the second half of that משנה. A cow taken over at a set price follows the one who took it, so a כהן who appraised an Israelite's cow may feed it תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like the later case: an Israelite who took a cow from a כהן at a set price may not feed it תרומה vetches, but a כהן who took a cow from an Israelite at a set price may feed it תרומה vetches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by pointing to the later case in the same משנה, which really does match guaranteed property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a cow is taken at an agreed price, the one who takes it carries the full risk, just like the husband with נכסי צאן ברזל. In that case the cow follows the one who took it for תרומה. So full responsibility is enough, and רב ספרא's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only like the later case (in the same משנה)
Took over at a set price, accepting full responsibility for its value

steps.whatToRemember: Full responsibility for something, where you carry every loss and gain, lets it eat תרומה like the כהן's own property, even without true ownership. Partial responsibility, like renting, does not. This is why רב ספרא can say guaranteed slaves eat תרומה while still belonging to the wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: It saves רב ספרא's reading. The משנה about guaranteed slaves eating תרומה no longer proves the husband owns them, which removes רב אמי's support.

phrases.english: This is only like the latter clause:
An Israelite who appraised a cow from a כהן
phrases.notes: "Appraised" means he took the cow at an agreed price and is responsible for its full value.

phrases.english: may not feed it vetches of תרומה.
But a כהן who appraised a cow from an Israelite
may feed it vetches of תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 6 by giving the correct comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a better matching case (the later case in the same משנה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rented cow seemed to show that only ownership lets an animal eat תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Full responsibility, as with an appraised cow or guaranteed property, is enough for eating תרומה even without ownership.

steps.title: Each side has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף note that there is a ברייתא supporting רב יהודה and another supporting רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף were sitting at the end of רב נחמן's lecture, and they said: There is a ברייתא that agrees with רב יהודה, and there is a ברייתא that agrees with רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next moves. It announces that each side has a ברייתא, and the next two steps will quote them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the debate rested on reading the משנה, and that reading was pushed back. Now the debate moves to a stronger kind of source: ברייתות that seem to back each side directly.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of his lecture

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef sat
at the end of Rav Nachman's lecture
and they sat and said:
It is taught in a baraita in agreement with Rav Yehuda,
and it is taught in a baraita in agreement with Rabbi Ami.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, וְתַנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over the משנה to ברייתות that support each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each opinion has a ברייתא supporting it.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: צאן ברזל slaves go free if the husband knocks out a tooth or an eye, but not if the wife does. This shows the husband counts as their owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא agrees with רבי אמי: צאן ברזל slaves go free through a tooth or an eye knocked out by the husband, but not by the wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first ברייתא, which backs רבי אמי's view that the slaves belong to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave goes free for a lost tooth or eye only when his owner caused the injury. Since the husband's blow frees the slave and the wife's blow does not, the husband must be the owner, just as רבי אמי said.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves the wife brings in as guaranteed property: the husband takes the risk and must return their set value
A tooth and an eye: if the owner knocks one out, the slave goes free

phrases.english: It is taught in agreement with Rabbi Ami:
Slaves of guaranteed property (tzon barzel)
go free through a tooth or an eye
phrases.notes: A slave whose owner knocks out his tooth or eye goes free, so whoever's blow frees him is treated as the owner.

phrases.english: caused by the husband, but not by the wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first ברייתא promised in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's view that צאן ברזל slaves belong to the husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the slaves go free through a tooth or eye knocked out by the husband but not by the wife.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The husband may not sell appraised property, even property he added from his own. If it was sold, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ruled the husband can take it back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא agrees with רב יהודה: If a woman brings appraised property into the marriage and the husband wants to sell it, he may not. Even if the husband added appraised property of his own to her dowry, he may not sell it. If one of them sold it for living expenses, such a case came before רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and he said the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא. It backs רב יהודה by showing that the husband does not fully own this property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the property were simply the husband's, he could sell it. The ברייתא says he cannot sell it, even what he himself added. It even lets him cancel his own sale and take the property back from the buyers. So the wife keeps a real hold on it, which fits רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Appraised property brought in at a set value (צאן ברזל)
Takes back from the hands of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the last line as punishing the buyers. It means the sale never took effect, because the property was not the husband's to sell.

phrases.english: It is taught in agreement with Rav Yehuda:
A woman who brings appraised property into the marriage for her husband,

phrases.aramaic: אִם רָצָה הַבַּעַל לִמְכּוֹר — לֹא יִמְכּוֹר.
phrases.english: if the husband wants to sell it, he may not sell it.
And not only that, but
even if he added appraised property of his own for her,

phrases.aramaic: אִם רָצָה הַבַּעַל לִמְכּוֹר — לֹא יִמְכּוֹר.
phrases.english: if the husband wants to sell it, he may not sell it.
If either of them sold it for living expenses,
there was such an incident

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and he said:
The husband takes it back from the buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ברייתא, this time backing רב יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that the wife keeps a real hold on צאן ברזל property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the husband may not sell appraised property, and a sale can be undone.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports in the name of רב נחמן that the הלכה follows רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה is like רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: With a ברייתא on each side, רב נחמן decides the practical הלכה in favor of רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ruling. The next steps test it, because רבי אמי also has a ברייתא behind him.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Nachman:
The halacha is like Rav Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the conflict between the two ברייתות in practice.

steps.title: רבא challenges the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן how he can rule like רב יהודה when a ברייתא supports רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: But there is a ברייתא that agrees with רבי אמי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the ruling and points to the ברייתא about tooth and eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling should not simply ignore a ברייתא. רבא wants to know what makes רב יהודה's side win when the other side has written support too.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
But isn't it taught in a baraita in agreement with Rabbi Ami!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא in step 9 supports רבי אמי, so why rule against him?

steps.title: רב יהודה's reason is more sensible
steps.stepSummary: Even though a ברייתא supports רבי אמי, רב יהודה's reason is more sensible, because of the honor of her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is a ברייתא that agrees with רבי אמי, רב יהודה's reason makes more sense, because of the honor of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that both sides have a ברייתא, but the reasoning behind רב יהודה's view is stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the sources are evenly split, the deciding factor is which reason is more sensible. Property from the wife's father's family brings that family honor, so she should be able to keep it and not just get money for it. That tips the scale to רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor of her father's house

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רב יהודה. A wife's צאן ברזל property is not simply the husband's to dispose of, because of שבח בית אביה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that when ברייתות conflict, the more sensible reason can decide the הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּתַנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Even though it is taught in agreement with Rabbi Ami,
Rav Yehuda's reason makes more sense,
because of the honor of her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּתַנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי, מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoning outweighs a conflicting source when the sources are split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ברייתא supporting רבי אמי should block ruling like רב יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides have a ברייתא, and רב יהודה's reason (שבח בית אביה) is more sensible, so the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: The story of the fine wool robe
steps.stepSummary: A woman brought a fine wool robe into her marriage, listed in her כתובה. Her husband died, and the orphans used it to cover his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman who brought her husband a fine wool robe, written into her כתובה. He died, and the orphans took the robe and spread it over the dead man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests the rule just decided. This step only sets up the case; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robe was guaranteed property listed in her כתובה. The orphans treated it as their father's and used it for his burial. The question will be whether she can claim it back.

phrases.english: A certain woman
brought in to her husband
a robe of fine wool, written into her ketubah.
He died,
the orphans took it
and spread it over the dead man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that applies the ruling about צאן ברזל property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of the robe; the ruling follows.

steps.title: רבא rules the dead man has acquired the robe
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the robe, once used to wrap the dead, belongs to the dead and cannot be returned to the widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The dead man has acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling on the robe case from the previous step: since it was used for the dead, the dead has acquired it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something used for a dead body becomes forbidden for anyone to benefit from. So once the orphans wrapped their father in the robe, the widow can no longer claim it back as part of her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rava said: The dead man has acquired it.
phrases.notes: He means the robe now belongs to the dead, and nobody may use or benefit from it anymore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the robe case described in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The robe used as a shroud belongs to the dead and is forbidden for benefit; the widow cannot reclaim it.

steps.title: Doesn't the הלכה follow רב יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: נאנאי asks רב כהנא how רבא can rule this way, when רבא himself reported that the הלכה follows רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: נאנאי, son of רב יוסף son of רבא, said to רב כהנא: But didn't רבא say in the name of רב נחמן that the הלכה follows רב יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רבא's ruling by pointing to his own earlier report that the הלכה follows רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה held that items a woman brought into the marriage go back to her, because of the honor of her father's house (step 13). If so, the robe should return to the widow, and the orphans should not have been able to make it the dead man's.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ נָאנַאי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Nanai, son of Rav Yosef,
son of Rava, said to Rav Kahana:
But didn't Rava say that Rav Nachman said:
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 11.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rav Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 15 using רבא's own report in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the dead has acquired the robe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the הלכה follows רב יהודה, the woman's items return to her, so the heirs should not be able to make the robe forbidden.

steps.title: Not yet collected, so still in the heirs' hands
steps.stepSummary: Even רב יהודה agrees that before she collects, the robe is still in the husband's possession, so the heirs could make it the dead man's.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: Doesn't רב יהודה agree that it has not yet been collected? And since it has not yet been collected, it is still in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered: רב יהודה's rule only matters once the widow actually collects; until then, the robe is still in the husband's domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה says what she brought goes back to her, but she still has to collect it. At the moment the robe was used for the dead, she had not collected it yet, so it was still under the husband's (and his heirs') control, and their use of it was valid.

keyTerms.meaning: still missing collection; not yet collected

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה is not being rejected here. His rule still stands; it just doesn't kick in until the woman actually collects.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי לָא מוֹדֶה רַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't Rav Yehuda agree
that it has not yet been collected?
And since it has not yet been collected,
it is still in his possession.
phrases.notes: "His" means the husband's, and after his death, his heirs'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא מוֹדֶה רַב יְהוּדָה דִּמְחוּסַּר גּוּבְיָינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רב יהודה's ruling to after collection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's rule means the robe was already the widow's, so the heirs couldn't make it the dead man's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before collection the robe is still in the husband's possession, so the heirs' use of it as a shroud took effect, and רבא's ruling fits רב יהודה.

steps.title: רבא is following his usual reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show that רבא's ruling fits his known principle, introducing a list that starts with הקדש and חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: הקדש, חמץ...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it begins quoting another statement of רבא to show his ruling here matches a principle he holds elsewhere. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "רבא לטעמיה" tells us this ruling is not a one-off; it comes from a consistent view of רבא. The list of items (הקדש, חמץ, and more) will show what that view is once the statement is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: according to his own reasoning; consistent with his view

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning, as Rava said:
Consecration, chametz,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבא's ruling in step 15 to a broader principle he states elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא is consistent with another statement of his, which begins with הקדש and חמץ and continues on the next amud.
